driving_question: The /x/ Minecraft-hunger-bar thread argues a God who is a hole in the system (hunger, absence, the thing that eats) is more coherent than a God who is a full object - is the hunger bar the better theology?
book: The Mystic Fable: Volume One (Michel de Certeau, 1981/1991)
best_collision: c02073 (de Certeau, the divine names the process by which the world is organized) vs c01968 (Campagna, Deus absconditus as the ground of the modern) @0.4789 complicates: both keep the absent God load-bearing, but de Certeau makes the absence a verb and Campagna a ground - the hole organizes (process) versus the hole supports (foundation). The hunger bar is c02073's cow: the absence that keeps the herd moving.
quote: If God does not exist, the cows are black and white; if God does exist, the cows are white and black. (p.101)
mutation_note: The thread asks whether the hunger bar (the God who is absence) is the better theology. de Certeau's corpus answers without naming games: the vanishing God was never the full object - it was the organizing absence, the 'nothing' that kept theology an infinite term. The hunger bar does not replace God; it is the cow whose coat proves the regime. Absence organizes; presence is what gets consumed. The /x/ thread's God is not more coherent than the object-God - it is the object-God's actual operating mode, and the bar is the index that never lies.
